result.rule: An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Use bpmn:subProcess for a nested workflow belonging to its parent process; keep all internal nodes and flows inside it.
For an event subprocess set triggeredByEvent=true, use exactly one triggered start event, and add no incoming or outgoing sequence flow.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
Keep each flow node and sequence flow inside its owning process or subprocess. Sequence flows never cross pool or subprocess boundaries.

result.rule: When the description identifies an ongoing process phase that is followed by a stated activity or outcome: Model the phase so that its sequence flow continues to the subsequent activity or outcome, using a gateway if the described control flow requires a decision or synchronization.

When the description says that an ongoing activity continues until a stated condition occurs, and then states an outcome that follows: Model waiting for that condition with an intermediate catch event, then continue the flow to the stated outcome.

When the description indicates that an activity recurs at intervals during a longer-running process phase.: Model the recurring activity as work within that phase and connect it to the surrounding process flow.
When the description states a process trigger followed by a subsequent activity: Connect the start event to the first activity with an outgoing sequence flow, preserving the stated execution order.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description assigns an action to a particular participant or distinguishes that action from related actions: label each corresponding BPMN element with the described action and responsible participant; do not substitute another actor or conflate it with a separate action

When the description states an activity together with a purpose, object, or scope that distinguishes what is being done: Label the corresponding BPMN task with its core action and enough of those stated details to preserve the activity’s meaning; do not add unsupported details or omit details that distinguish it.

When the description states an activity and lists multiple purposes or criteria for it: Label the corresponding task with the core activity and its stated object; do not narrow the label to just one of the listed purposes or criteria.

When the description names components included in a broader process stage but does not specify the action performed for each component: label each corresponding activity neutrally with the stated component; do not imply that someone provides, performs, or completes it unless the description supports that action
